comparator.name: Bachelor Industrial Design
comparator.sourceNotes: TU/e's current official programme, degree-structure, department and Education Guide pages, checked 2026-10-03, describe a three-year, 180-EC Industrial Design bachelor built around intelligent and interactive products, design projects, competency development and an individually developed designer identity. The programme integrates five expertise areas—User & Society, Technology & Realization, Math, Data & Computing, Business & Entrepreneurship, and Creativity & Aesthetics—through courses, repeated multidisciplinary design projects, coaching and a Bachelor Final Project. The components below retain the complete 60-EC load of each study year without inventing individual credits that the public curriculum overview does not print.
components: Year 1: foundations, core expertise-area courses and design projects
Foundational development across the five expertise areas, design and research methods, professional skills, prototyping and coached multidisciplinary project work.
Year 2: advanced competency development, electives and design projects

Further courses and project work in user-centred interaction, intelligent products, data and computing, technology realisation, aesthetics, business, entrepreneurship and responsible design, with genuine room for an individual profile.
Year 3: individual profile, electives, Impact of Technology and Bachelor Final Project
Advanced individual competency development and an integrating Bachelor Final Project in which the student demonstrates the programme's design, technology, research and professional competencies.

exception.reason: TU/e Industrial Design is a cumulative studio- and project-based technology-design degree. Students repeatedly integrate user and society research, technology realisation, mathematics/data/computing, business and entrepreneurship, and creativity and aesthetics while building and testing intelligent interactive products, reflecting on competency growth and developing an individual designer identity before a Bachelor Final Project. UCR offers one substantive consumer-product-design course and useful adjacent study in entrepreneurship, consumer research, psychology, computing, data, AI, robotics, sustainability and creative communication. It does not offer the repeated industrial- and interaction-design studio spine, physical-computing and interactive-electronics sequence, sensor integration and digital-fabrication laboratories, interaction aesthetics and visualisation progression, iterative user-testing studios, coached design-competency portfolio or equivalent Industrial Design final project. A 24-course UCR response would be an interdisciplinary liberal-arts programme with one product-design experience and several adjacent subjects, not a defensible Industrial Design comparator.
exception.curriculumContext: The current official programme accounts for a three-year, 180-EC bachelor and organises each 60-EC year around progressive competency development. The curriculum integrates five expertise areas—User & Society; Technology & Realization; Math, Data & Computing; Business & Entrepreneurship; and Creativity & Aesthetics—with design and research processes and professional skills. Students learn through core and elective courses, multidisciplinary projects, coaching, reflection and portfolio development, progressively combining user observation and testing, interaction and behavioural design, programming and data, physical computing and sensors, rapid prototyping and digital fabrication, product aesthetics, systems thinking, sustainability, business propositions and responsible innovation. The Bachelor Final Project requires those competencies to be integrated in an independently shaped intelligent or interactive product, system or service rather than treated as unrelated electives.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. BENENTR111 Consumer Product Design is the closest substantive course: students investigate customer needs, develop a product concept and fabrication method, build a prototype, model quantitatively and assess sustainability, costs and intellectual property. BENGATE101 Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, BENENTR211 Marketing & Consumer Engagement, BENENTR212 Strategy & Digital Transformation, BENENTR311 Market Research and BENLEAD311 Psychology of Organizations & Leadership add business, customer and innovation perspectives. HCBPSYC111 Social Psychology and HCBCOGN212 Perception & Action provide relevant human-behaviour foundations. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming, DISCOMP213 Software Development, DISDATA111 Introduction to Data Science, DISDATA212 Image Processing & Computer Vision, DISDATA311 Neural Networks & Deep Learning and DISDATA312 Robotics provide computation, intelligent-systems and perception capabilities. ENSGATE101 Sustainability Essentials I, ENSSUST112 Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design provide sustainability perspectives, while MCCCOMM312 Creative Communication Laboratory supports creative media practice. The workbook nevertheless contains no industrial- or interaction-design studio sequence, design drawing and visualisation progression, aesthetics-of-interaction studio, physical-computing and interactive-electronics laboratory, sensor and actuator integration, digital fabrication, materials and manufacturing progression, repeated prototype-and-user-test cycle, service-design studio, coached competency portfolio, or Industrial Design Bachelor Final Project. BENENTR111 is one valuable product-development course but cannot replace three years of cumulative projects integrating users, electronics, fabrication, data, aesthetics and business. The available UCR courses support a technology-and-design theme while leaving the target programme's defining studio, realisation, interaction and capstone formation unmatched.
